What each supplies, as recorded in the pinned ledger:

- **`RVI-INTRO`** — execution-environment interface (EEI) and hart definitions; the four trap effects; the meaning of UNSPECIFIED
- **`RVI-RV32I`** — the base integer ISA that RV64I modifies: register state, formats, control transfer, load/store, FENCE, ECALL/EBREAK, HINTs
- **`RVI-RV64I`** — the RV64I deltas: XLEN=64, the *W instruction family, 6-bit shift amounts, LWU/LD/SD, RV64I HINT table
- **`RVI-NAMING`** — the G abbreviation's definition (IMAFDZicsr_Zifencei), the extension naming/ordering rules the ISA string follows, and the dependency-discipline context for the closure
- **`RVI-G-LISTING`** — the RV32/64G instruction set listings and the base opcode map — the reference each extension's instruction census is drawn from in the evidence leaves
- **`RVI-M`** — the M extension: multiply/divide semantics, the *W forms, division-by-zero and overflow conventions
- **`RVI-A`** — the A extension: LR/SC reservation semantics, the AMO operations, the aq/rl ordering annotations
- **`RVI-F`** — the F extension: f0–f31 and the FP CSRs, single-precision arithmetic under IEEE 754-2008, and the stated dependency on Zicsr
- **`RVI-D`** — the D extension: FLEN=64 widening, NaN boxing, double-precision arithmetic — and the stated dependency on F
- **`RVI-C`** — the C extension: 16-bit encodings, IALIGN=16 with C, the alignment-exception consequence
- **`RVI-ZC`** — the C decomposition: C implies Zca always, Zcf only at RV32 with F, Zcd when D is present — the closure's C leg
- **`RVI-ZICSR`** — the six CSR instructions (csrrw/csrrs/csrrc and immediates), the read/write side-effect discipline, and the counter-CSR access rules
- **`RVI-ZIFENCEI`** — FENCE.I: when newly written code becomes executable — the instruction-visibility contract the rv64i profile deliberately excluded
- **`RVI-ZICNTR`** — the Zicntr base counters (cycle, time, instret) — the S-mode time read a Linux profile needs; Zihpm (performance counters) is named here and NOT selected
- **`RVI-RVWMO`** — the RVWMO memory consistency model — the memory-model claim this profile makes (the A extension's atomics make it load-bearing even at one hart)
- **`RVP-INTRO`** — the privileged architecture's introduction: the privilege modes and their intent, the platform-level sweep
- **`RVP-CSR`** — the CSR address-space conventions, the listings, the WPRI/WARL/WLRL field disciplines the privilege leaf (P4-SYSTEM.2) owns
- **`RVP-MACHINE`** — the machine-level ISA: the M-mode CSRs, the trap model (medeleg/mideleg included), the counter machinery, the optional PMP (§2.1.7), mret/wfi
- **`RVP-SUPERVISOR`** — the supervisor-level ISA: the S-mode CSRs, satp, and the three paged schemes at SXLEN=64 (Sv39 §11.1.4, Sv48 §11.1.5, Sv57 §11.1.6)
- **`RVP-INSNS`** — the privileged instruction listings — the reference the privileged-instruction census is drawn from in the evidence leaves
- **`RVP-SSTC`** — Sstc: the stimecmp CSR and the menvcfg.STCE gate — the S-mode timer without an M-mode round trip
- **`RVI-PSABI`** — the toolchain-output contract: the calling convention, and the LP64D statement — the standard RV64G ABI requires D (hardware floating-point calling convention, ABI_FLEN=64)
- **`RVI-SBI`** — the M-mode firmware contract for the P6 boot route: the base extension plus TIME, sPI, RFENCE, HSM, SRST, DBCN — the services a Linux boot needs
- **`SIFIVE-FU540-C000`** — the implemented-precedent leg for the Sv39 selection: the U54's MMU supports Bare and Sv39 (§4.7) and raises page faults rather than setting PTE A/D bits — the A/D-policy data point P4-SYSTEM.3 inherits
